title: Design and validate assessment, test, and audit strategies
summary: A sound strategy defines the decision, scope, criteria, independence, method, evidence, schedule, and limits before work begins.
outcome: Choose an assessment strategy for a stated control question and explain its scope, criteria, evidence, independence, and limitations.
managerMindset: A method is only credible when it answers a defined question within an explicit scope.

sections.title: Separate assessment, test, and audit
sections.body: An assessment evaluates controls or processes against criteria and produces evidence about risk or effectiveness. A test executes a defined procedure to produce observable results about a control, system, or behavior. An audit is an independent, systematic examination against agreed criteria, with formal evidence and reporting expectations. They may use overlapping techniques but are not interchangeable labels.
keyPoints: Assessment is the broad decision activity; testing is a method; audit emphasizes independence and criteria.
Scope and objectives prevent irrelevant evidence collection.
Validation checks that the strategy can answer the intended question.

sections.title: Design for useful evidence
sections.body: Set boundaries, population, sampling, timing, assumptions, roles, rules of engagement, evidence handling, safety constraints, and reporting recipients. Select qualitative or quantitative measures appropriate to the decision. State exclusions and residual uncertainty so a clean result cannot be mistaken for proof that an unexamined area is safe.
keyPoints: Criteria must be observable and mapped to requirements or risk.
Independence and conflicts of interest should be addressed before evidence collection.
A narrow test can be rigorous without supporting a broad conclusion.

sections.title: Match independence and location to the assurance question
sections.body: Internal work benefits from context and continuous access but may face reporting or familiarity bias; external assessors can add independence and specialized skill; third-party reviews examine a provider or service outside enterprise control and require contract, scope, and complementary-control analysis. Define whether the population is on-premises, cloud, hybrid, or provider-operated, including regions, interfaces, inherited controls, and evidence access. Independence is a managed property of reporting line, conflicts, competence, and decision authority—not a label alone.
keyPoints: Scope must include physical, virtual, provider, and inherited boundaries.
Cloud evidence needs customer/provider responsibility and location assumptions.
Disclose conflicts and set escalation or independent review before fieldwork.

workedExamples.title: Cloud access review
workedExamples.situation: Leadership asks whether privileged cloud access is safe.
workedExamples.reasoning: Define accounts, roles, regions, time window, control criteria, evidence sources, sampling, assessor independence, and report decision. A password scan alone cannot answer the governance and lifecycle question.

distinctions.difference: Assessment evaluates against a question and risk; test executes a procedure; audit independently examines against criteria.

misconceptions.misconception: A penetration test is the same as an audit.
misconceptions.correction: A penetration test explores technical exploitability; an audit evaluates evidence against defined criteria and independence requirements.

recallChecks.prompt: What must be fixed before selecting a method?
recallChecks.answer: The decision question, scope, criteria, evidence needs, and constraints.
They bound the conclusion and prevent overclaiming assurance.

scenarioSeeds.scenario: A manager requests a full-security conclusion from a one-day vulnerability scan.
scenarioSeeds.decision: Narrow the conclusion to the scanned scope and method, or design a broader program.
scenarioSeeds.why: Evidence cannot support claims beyond population, time, and method.

studyPlan.learn: Contrast assessment, test, and audit and study strategy design.
studyPlan.connect: Connect scope to D1 risk and D7 evidence sources.
studyPlan.apply: Write a strategy for one access control.
studyPlan.revisit: Identify the unsupported claims in a broad executive statement.

review.notes: Independent AI review only. Claim evidence, exact content fingerprints, scope checks, visual and memory-map assessments are recorded in knowledge/quality/. No human expert review or exam-readiness claim.

visualLearningContract.teachingQuestion: Which assurance activity, scope, criteria, and independence are credible for this claim?
visualLearningContract.misconception: Any scan or auditor report proves control effectiveness.
visualLearningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
visualLearningContract.focalInsight: Assessment informs; test exercises; audit evaluates criteria/evidence independently.
visualLearningContract.retrievalPrompt: Provider report exists but customer configuration is excluded: what scope gap remains?
visualLearningContract.textFallback:
assessment: evaluate state/risk. Decision: select assessment question. Failure/example: risk inferred from checklist
test: exercise expected behavior. Decision: authorize safe test. Failure/example: production outage
audit: criteria/evidence evaluation. Decision: set independence. Failure/example: self-audit conflict
scope: included systems/locations/period. Decision: bound claim. Failure/example: cloud tenant omitted
criteria: standard/control expectation. Decision: define pass evidence. Failure/example: undefined pass
independence: freedom from conflict. Decision: separate reviewer. Failure/example: operator validates own control
